title: each and every
subtitle: each book / every book
summary: Use each when you think of things separately, one by one, and every when you think of them as a group - and learn the structures that go with each of them.

lesson.heading: each or every?

left.label: each = one by one
left.text: We think of the things separately. Each is more usual for a small number.
examples: There were four books on the table. **Each** book was a different colour.
At the beginning of the game, **each** player has three cards.

right.label: every = all of them
right.text: We think of the things as a group. Every is more usual for a large number.
examples: **Every** window in the house was open.
Kate loves reading. She has read **every** book in the library.
I'd like to visit **every** country in the world.

lesson.note: Often either word is possible: **Each** time I see you, you look different. or **Every** time I see you ...

lesson.heading: each for two; every for how often
lesson.text: We use **each** (not every) when we are talking about two things. And we use **every** (not each) to say how often something happens.

examples.text: In football, **each** team has eleven players.
'How often do you use your car?' '**Every** day.'
The Olympic Games are held **every** four years.

lesson.heading: The structures

left.label: each
left.text: We can use each with or without a noun.
examples: None of the rooms are the same. **Each room** is different.
**Each** is different. or **Each one** is different.
**Each of** the books was a different colour.
**Each of** them was a different colour.

right.label: every
right.text: We use every with a noun - never alone.
examples: She's read **every book** in the library.
*A:* Have you read all these books? *B:* Yes, **every one**.
I've read **every one of** those books.

lesson.note: We say each of the books (not ~~each of books~~) and every one of those books (not ~~every of those books~~).

lesson.heading: each in the middle of a sentence
lesson.text: **Each** can also come in the middle of a sentence, after the subject or after the verb *be*. We also say **a dollar each**, **ten pounds each** etc.

examples.text: The students **were each given** a book.
examples.note: = Each student was given a book.

examples.text: We paid 200 dollars **each**. or We **each** paid 200 dollars.

lesson.heading: everyone or every one?
lesson.text: **Everyone** (one word) is only for people and means *everybody*. **Every one** (two words) is for things or people and means *each one*.

examples.text: Sarah is invited to lots of parties and she goes to **every one**.
I dropped a tray of glasses. Unfortunately **every one** broke.

lesson.text: A quick test: if you could say all instead, every is usually right; if you are picking things out one by one, use each.

exercises.prompt: There were four books on the table. ___ book was a different colour.
exercises.explanation: Four is a small number and we look at the books one by one, so each is more natural.

exercises.prompt: 'How often do you use your car?' '___ day.'
exercises.explanation: We use every, not each, to say how often something happens.

exercises.prompt: There are six apartments in the building. ___ one has a balcony.
exercises.explanation: We are looking at the apartments separately, one by one: each one.

exercises.prompt: Does each sentence need each or every in the gap (shown as ...)?

items.text: ... side of a square is the same length.
... seat in the theatre was taken.
There's a train to London ... hour.
She was wearing four rings - one on ... finger.
In football, ... team has eleven players.
Our football team is playing well. We've won ... game this season.
The Olympic Games are held ... four years.

exercises.explanation: We mean parents as a group, like all parents, so we use every.

exercises.prompt: The book is divided into five parts and ___ these has three sections.
exercises.explanation: Before the/these/them we say each of: each of these.

exercises.prompt: A friend of mine has three children. I always give ___ them a present at Christmas.
exercises.explanation: Each of them - we think of the children one by one.

exercises.prompt: Every student in the class was given a book. Say this with each in the middle of the sentence.
exercises.answer: The students were each given a book
exercises.explanation: Each can go in the middle of the sentence: The students were each given a book.

exercises.prompt: The price of one of those oranges is 40 pence. Those oranges are 40 pence ___.
exercises.explanation: We say 40 pence each = 40 pence for one orange.

exercises.prompt: I had ten pounds and so did Sonia. Sonia and I had ten pounds ___.
exercises.explanation: Each at the end means each of us had ten pounds.

exercises.statement: Amy is very popular. Every one likes her.
exercises.explanation: Amy is very popular. Everyone likes her. For people in general we use everyone as one word.

exercises.prompt: Sarah is invited to a lot of parties and she goes to ___.
exercises.explanation: Every one (two words) = every party. Everyone as one word is only for people.
